card.category: torrent index API (The Pirate Bay, JSON, no key)
card.summary: No key and no account: GET /q.php?q=ubuntu&cat=0 returned 27,772 bytes of JSON with id, name, info_hash, seeders, leechers, size and category for every hit.

record.category: torrent index API (The Pirate Bay, JSON, no key)

free_tier.stated: No key and no account: GET /q.php?q=ubuntu&cat=0 returned 27,772 bytes of JSON with id, name, info_hash, seeders, leechers, size and category for every hit.

retention.stated: the index keeps the row after the swarm dies; seeders and leechers are the only liveness signal in the record

egress.terms: no byte allowance: JSON only; the transfer is between the user and the swarm

record.interface_detail: GET /q.php?q=<query>&cat=<n> returns a JSON array; every row carries info_hash so a magnet is one string concatenation away. Responses are front-cached (Cache-Control max-age=7200).
record.tooling: One GET and a json parse; the whole site is a thin client over this API, so a scraper of the HTML is pointless.
record.chaining: Search by title, build the magnet from info_hash, then ask a debrid service for a cache hit before pulling anything.

limits.value: none published; 10 status-checked requests plus 10 more over 55 s all returned 200, with no 429 and no Retry-After

record.limits_note: robots.txt on apibay.org carries only Cloudflare content signals and no crawl delay. The 7,200-second cache means repeated identical queries cost the origin nothing.
record.binding_note: No byte quota exists on an index; the only constraint is the rate at which titles are enumerated, and it tolerated about 0.2 req/s with no throttle.

identity_cost.detail: No key, no account, no captcha. The site's own 'robot check' overlays are ad furniture, not an API gate.

record.reliability_note: The API is served through Cloudflare with a two-hour cache, so a query can answer from cache after the swarm has gone; single-file rows report num_files 1 and a size in bytes, which is enough to filter but not to confirm the file still exists.
record.confidence_note: A live query was executed and its JSON read on 2026-10-23. A recorded probe over an hour would raise the rate row to measured.

evidence.proved: HTTP 200 application/json, 27,772 bytes, rows with info_hash, seeders, leechers, size in bytes and category id
content-signal text only, with no crawl delay and no rate limit stated

record.notes: The cleanest no-account JSON torrent feed found: a single GET, a fixed schema, and an info hash in every row. Its political fragility is the risk, not its quota: the domain is one seizure away from gone.
